questions.answer: If he holds on, yes. Andrea Kimi Antonelli would be 20 at the finale, 3 years younger than Sebastian Vettel's record.
questions.body: Andrea Kimi Antonelli leads the 2026 championship and turns 20 before the last race. The youngest champion so far is Sebastian Vettel, who won in 2010 at 23 years and 134 days. Our title model gives Antonelli more than 99% from here.
questions.q: Is Andrea Kimi Antonelli about to be the youngest champion ever?

questions.answer: Not yet. At Ferrari he wins 2% of races against 34% at Mercedes, and Leclerc has beaten him 28 times to 13.
questions.body: Mercedes from 2013 to 2024 against Ferrari since 2025. Points per race use each race's own scoring.
questions.q: Did Hamilton's move to Ferrari actually work?

questions.answer: Yes, at the top. Mercedes gained +14.5 points a race, McLaren dropped 14.8.
questions.body: Points per race in 2025 against 2026, so a full season compares fairly with one still running. Sauber is counted as Audi.
questions.q: Did the 2026 rules flip the grid?

questions.answer: Hamilton's 2007 is still the rookie season to beat. Antonelli's first year sits between him and a teenage Verstappen.
questions.body: Each driver's first full season. Points are re-scored on today's 25-18-15 system so 2007 and 2015 compare fairly. Hamilton started in a front-running McLaren, Verstappen at 17 in a Toro Rosso.
questions.q: Rookie Antonelli vs rookie Hamilton vs rookie Verstappen

questions.answer: Yes. 19 wins from 22 races, led 76% of all laps, and a title margin of 50% of his own points.
questions.body: Ranked by the share of races the champion won. Early seasons count the Indy 500, which was part of the championship then.

chart.title: Share of races won by the champion

questions.q: Was Verstappen's 2023 the most dominant season ever?

questions.answer: Lewis Hamilton, gaining 1.5 places a race more than a typical driver from the same grid slot.
questions.body: Every classified finish in 2025 and 2026. Starting further back makes gains easier, so each result is measured against the average gain from that grid position. At least 15 finishes.
questions.q: Who's the best overtaker on today's grid?

questions.answer: Less than it feels. 45 of 87 races since 2023 had a safety car or red flag, and the leader when it came out lost the win 7 times.
questions.body: Leader means whoever was first at the end of the lap before the first full safety car or red flag. Virtual safety cars aren't counted, they rarely change the order.

chart.title: Races where the safety car changed the winner

questions.answer: Mercedes have the quickest stops this year and sit P1 in the standings. Pit speed and results are strongly linked.
questions.body: Median time in the pit lane for each team's stops in 2026, entry to exit, so it includes the drive through the lane. The rank match between pit speed and championship place is 0.90 (1 would be a perfect match). Fast teams tend to be good at both, so it shows the best teams pit well, not that pit stops win titles.

chart.title: Median pit lane time (and championship place)

questions.q: Does the fastest pit crew actually win anything?

questions.answer: Yuki Tsunoda, with a 71-lap stint. And one-stop wins are the most common: 46% of races since 2023.
questions.body: The longest single set of tyres in a race since 2023, checked against the official pit stop records. Monaco fills the top because it barely wears tyres and overtaking is close to impossible, so teams stretch stints there. Races with a red flag are left out, since teams can change tyres for free during the stoppage.

questions.answer: Yes. Pole wins 59% of races in the 2020s, the highest of any decade (the 2000s were 49%).
questions.body: How often the driver on pole won the race, by decade. Pole is the fastest qualifier, or the pole sitter on the grid where qualifying records are missing.
questions.q: Is pole worth more than ever?

questions.answer: Charles Leclerc. Retirements cost about 55 points in 2025–26, counting where he was running when it ended.
questions.body: For each retirement, the points the driver would have scored holding the place they had on their last lap, on today's 25-18-15 scale. It can't tell a crash from a car failure, the official records rarely say.
questions.q: Who's lost the most points to retirements?
